chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When the Muhrim (person in Ihram) scratches his head, lice and dandruff fall off from him.' He said: 'There is no penalty upon him, and it does not count as repeating (the act).' I said: 'How does he scratch his head?' He said: 'With his fingernails, as long as he does not cause bleeding and does not cut the hair.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.وَلَا يَعُودُ: And it does not repeat/count again

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muhrim scratching their head to remove lice or dandruff?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that scratching the head to remove lice or dandruff does not break Ihram nor incur a penalty, provided the method is gentle. The specific condition is that one must use fingernails without causing bleeding or cutting the hair, distinguishing minor grooming from acts that nullify the state of consecration. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on ease and the distinction between intentional violation and natural relief in the laws of Hajj.
